reviewer.actual_effort: Read current.json, current.review.xml and guideline-excerpts.md in full. Opened all 9 row crops for s168, s170 and s172, and rows 1–3 of s174 (the rest of s174 is haftarah material outside scope). Did not open the native s168–s174 JPGs, the English pages s169–s175, the primary JSON or the independent blind JSONs. Ran no validator, compiler, refdb or versification tool. At crop resolution I could match consonants, maqaf, sof pasuq, paseq, verse order and the shape of most accents, but I could not certify every meteg or small conjunctive accent.

issues: Wrong order in the cue between 21:21 and 21:22 (s170-row8). Reading right to left, the print has 'מִצְרָֽיִם׃ פ ד. (בשבת ו.)': the open-paragraph mark פ comes first, then the aliyah label ד., then the Shabbat label. The encoding has 'ד. פ (בשבת ו.)'. Fix it to the printed order.

Separate cues are packed into single notes. The open-paragraph mark פ, the weekday aliyah numbers (ג., ד., ה.) and the parenthesised Shabbat-only aliyah labels '(בשבת ג.)', '(בשבת ד.)', '(בשבת ה.)', '(בשבת ו.)', '(בשבת ז.)' are each separate printed cues. Under the guideline's rubric rules the '(בשבת …)' labels say when a break applies, so they are conditions, not descriptions. They should not share one tei:note type='description' with the weekday number or the פ mark (after 21:12, 21:21 and 21:27).

Possible missing meteg in 21:9 on יָלְדָ֥ה (s168-row9, last word on the left). Under yod I see a qamats followed by a vertical stroke, the same pattern as 21:3 יָֽלְדָה־לּ֥וֹ (s168-row6), which is encoded with a meteg. The encoding has יָלְדָ֥ה without one. Confidence is moderate at this resolution, so it is also listed under unresolved.

A Hebrew source cue is not encoded anywhere in this module: s168-row5, centred above 21:1, 'וקורין בס״ת ראשון וה׳ פקד את שרה בפרשת וירא.' (approximate reading of a small font). It is a ritual instruction and belongs in the service order, not inside the reusable verse text. I did not check whether the service spine already has it.
unresolved: 21:1 וַֽיהוָ֛ה (s168-row5, first word on the right): the encoding has a meteg on the vav. There is a mark under the vav next to the patach, but I could not tell whether it is a meteg.

21:2 וַתַּ֩הַר֩ (s168-row6): I see two telisha qetana circles, one over the middle of the word and one over the resh. The encoding has U+05A9 twice. I could not see which letter the first circle sits on.
21:3 אֶֽת־שֶׁם־בְּנ֧וֹ: the encoding has a meteg on the alef of אֶֽת. That word ends s168-row6 and I could not see a meteg there.
21:3 הַנּֽוֹלַד־ל֛וֹ (s168-row6): the encoding has a meteg on the nun. Unclear in the crop.
21:9 יָלְדָ֥ה (s168-row9): possible meteg on the yod (see issues).
21:14 וַיִּֽקַּֽח־לֶ֩חֶם֩ (s170-row3): the encoding has two metegs, on the yod and on the qof. I could not separate them from the vowels.

21:16 אָֽמְרָ֔ה (s170-row5), 21:30 תִּֽהְיֶה־לִּ֣י (s172-row4), 21:13 and 21:18 כִּֽי־ (s170-row3, s170-row6), 21:7 כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי (s168-row8), 21:6 יִֽצְחַק־לִֽי (s168-row8), 21:14 וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֶ֑הָ (s170-row4), 21:22 וַֽיְהִי֙ (s170-row8): the meteg on the first syllable of each is encoded. In each crop a mark is plausibly there, but I could not confirm it letter by letter.

21:23 בֵֽאלֹהִים֙ (s170-row9): the encoding has a meteg under the bet. The print uses the font's alef-lamed ligature here. I read it as plain alef + lamed, as encoded, not as damage. I could not confirm the meteg.

21:6 צְחֹ֕ק (s168-row7) and 21:12 בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ (s170-row2): the accents are present in the print, but I could not distinguish zaqef gadol from other marks, or confirm the doubled pashta on the second letter versus the last letter.

Beyond the entries above, I did not compare every conjunctive accent (munach, mahpakh, merkha, darga, qadma) and every meteg in 21:1–34 glyph by glyph. Consonants, maqaf, sof pasuq, paseq (21:14, 21:17), disjunctive accent shapes and verse order did match in the crops.
verified: Extent: 21:1–34 runs continuously from s168-row5 to s172-row6, ending 'רַבִּֽים׃ פ'. complete_chapters genesis/21 is justified by the print. The blessings before and after on s168 are outside the encoding, as required.
Verse order 1–34 matches the print. No verses are missing or repeated.

Page breaks: 21:9 breaks after אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה (end of s168) / לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם (start of s170), and 21:23 breaks after וּלְנִינִ֖י (end of s170) / וּלְנֶכְדִּ֑י (start of s172). Both match the encoded tei:pb, with n=73/74/75 and facs n167/n169/n171.

Cue positions match the print: 'לוי.' between 21:4 and 21:5 (s168-row7), '(בשבת ג.)' before 21:9 (s168-row9), 'ג. (בשבת ד.)' after 21:12 (s170-row3), '(בשבת ה.)' after 21:17 (s170-row6), 'ה. (בשבת ז.)' after 21:27 (s172-row3), and final פ after 21:34 (s172-row6). Each sits outside verse scope behind a bare verse terminator, so the aliyah labels are independent of the verse milestones.
Paseq is printed and encoded in 21:14 (אַבְרָהָ֣ם ׀ בַּבֹּ֡קֶר) and 21:17 (אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ אֶל־הָגָר֙). The gershayim accent on 21:26 וְגַם־אַתָּ֞ה is present (s172-row2).
Consonants and maqaf match the print word for word in all rows I examined. I found no sic/corr or qere/ketiv in the body and none is needed. I found no printed consonantal error.
The divine name is marked at 21:1 (twice) and 21:33. Canonical verse URNs are reused and no new identities are created.

English: corresp keys for 21:1–34 match the Hebrew one to one. The chapter milestone has a corresp and both sides close with bare verse and chapter terminators. English page splits are in 21:9 (s169/s171) and 21:23 (s171/s173). I did not change or translate any text.

issues: The opening '<tei:milestone unit="chapter" n="29"/>' (Hebrew and English) has @unit but no @corresp. By guideline rule 3 that makes it a terminator, not a chapter opener, yet it carries @n. It correctly avoids claiming the whole of chapter 29, but it is misleading markup: either remove it, or drop @n. The trailing bare chapter milestone also closes nothing that was opened.

Source cues around the reading are not in this module. Before 29:1, at s172-row7: 'מניחים ס״ת שני אצל הראשון ואומרים חצי קדיש על שניהם, ומגביהים וגוללים ס״ת שקראו בו, ופותחים ס״ת ב׳ וקוראים בו למפטיר בפ׳ פינחס.' After 29:6, at s174-row2: 'מי שברך. ומגביהין וגוללין. כשמגביהין הס״ת מביטין נגד הכתב של ס״ת ואומרים:'. These are ritual instructions for the service order. I did not check whether the spine has them.
unresolved: 29:6 לַיהוָֽה׃ (s174-row2): the encoding has no meteg on the lamed, while 29:2 לַֽיהוָ֔ה (s172-row8) is encoded with one. There is a mark under the lamed in 29:6 that I could not tell apart from the patach.
29:1 יִהְיֶ֣ה (first occurrence, s172-row7, end of line): I could not confirm munach versus some other conjunctive accent.
29:1 מִֽקְרָא־קֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ (s172-row7): could not confirm the meteg on the mem or the doubled pashta.
29:3 וּמִ֨נְחָתָ֔ם (s172-row8, end of line): could not confirm qadma on the mem.
Beyond these, I did not compare every conjunctive accent and meteg in 29:1–6 glyph by glyph. Consonants, maqaf, mappiq in וּמִנְחָתָהּ (twice, 29:6), telisha on מִלְּבַד֩ and sof pasuq did match.
verified: Extent: the print runs only 29:1–6, from s172-row7 to s174-row2, ending at לַיהוָֽה׃. The encoding's start/end (numbers/29/1 to numbers/29/6) bound it correctly, and complete_chapters is rightly absent.
Page break: 29:3 ends s172 at לָאָֽיִל׃ and 29:4 begins s174 at וְעִשָּׂר֣וֹן. This matches the encoded tei:pb n=75 → n=76 (facs n171 → n173).
Verse order 1–6 matches the print. Consonants and maqaf match (וּשְׂעִיר־ at the end of s174-row1, עִזִּ֥ים at the start of row 2).
The divine name is marked in 29:2 and 29:6. I found no sic/corr or qere/ketiv in the body and none is needed.

English: corresp keys for 29:1–6 match the Hebrew one to one. English 29:4 starts on s173 ('and one tenth') and continues on s175. That is only a page-position difference from the Hebrew, not a misalignment. I did not change or translate any text.
